overview: This House resolution holds Michael Joseph in contempt of Congress for refusing to comply with two subpoenas the House Ethics Committee issued to him on September 11, 2025: one ordering him to hand over documents and one ordering him to testify. The Ethics Committee is the House panel that investigates possible misconduct, and its investigative subcommittee had sought his records and testimony. The resolution directs the Speaker of the House to send the committee's report on his refusal to the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, the federal prosecutor who can bring criminal charges for contempt of Congress under federal law. It also tells the Speaker to take any other appropriate steps to enforce the subpoenas. The House adopted it on September 1, 2026.
for: Supporters say congressional subpoenas mean little if people can ignore them without consequence, and referring the matter to prosecutors protects the Ethics Committee's ability to investigate misconduct.
against: Critics say contempt referrals are a heavy step that can expose a private person to criminal charges, and that disputes over subpoenas might be better resolved through negotiation or the courts first.
